title: Operational Playbook: Unified Runloop and Postmortem Rubric
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary

This playbook defines a single, auditable runloop for incidents at Redwood Inference that unifies: on-call rotations, bridge/bridge-operator responsibilities, runbook-driven remediation steps, game-day simulations, status page messaging, and a measurable postmortem quality rubric. The goal is predictable, low-friction incident handling and continuous improvement across SRE, Serving, and Platform teams.

Audience and scope
- Primary: SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, and Core Product engineers on pager.
- Secondary: Support/Customer Success for customer comms and account escalation.
- Applies to: service availability, latency SLO regressions, data-path correctness (prefix/KV cache), capacity exhaustion, and control plane failures.

Key definitions
- Runloop Operator: the person running the live bridge, responsible for status updates and coordination.
- Bridge Channel: #incident-ops (Slack) and dedicated Zoom bridge.
- Tiered SLO classes: Critical (SLO 99.99), High (99.95), Standard (99.9).
- Severity mapping:
  1. Sev0 — complete outage for >= 5% customers or global control-plane failure.
  2. Sev1 — significant degradation (P95 latency > 2x SLO or error rate causing user-visible failures).
  3. Sev2 — partial impact to subset of customers or non-critical functionality.

Incident lifecycle (high-level runloop)
1) Acknowledge (0-5 minutes)
   - Pagered engineer acknowledges in-monitoring alert and posts in #incident-ops with short summary: service, symptoms, first-detected timestamp.
   - Runloop Operator opens incident in our incident tracker (use template: incident.create --service <name> --class <Critical|High|Standard>).
2) Triage and classification (5-15 minutes)
   - Confirm scope (region, model family, customer subset).
   - Map to SLO class and set severity. If severity escalation is needed, page SRE lead and product on-call.
3) Containment (15-60 minutes)
   - Execute targeted runbook for the symptom (see example runbooks below).
   - If no runbook exists, capture steps attempted and enable mitigation flags (traffic shaping, heavier caching, temporary fallback model) per policy.
4) Restoration (30-180 minutes)
   - Restore service incrementally where possible. Validate with synthetic traffic and user-facing checks.
   - Update status page (see templates) every 30 minutes for critical incidents until mitigated.
5) Remediation and fix tracking (within 72 hours)
   - Assign remediation owner and open a ticket in the remediation tracker. High-severity incidents require a remediation plan within 7 calendar days.
6) Post-incident review (within 3 business days)
   - Postmortem draft in Confluence using the template in this doc. Use the Postmortem Quality Rubric for acceptance.

Runbook examples (copyable templates)
- Symptom: Regional 5xx spike for model inference (Region: us-west-2)\  1. Verify metrics: errors by model, host, and region (cli: redwood-metrics query --metric inference_errors --by host,model,region).\  2. If host-level error rate > 20% for a host group, drain new requests from that host pool: redwood-ctl pool drain --pool <pool-id>.\  3. If KV-cache errors visible in logs, flip prefix-cache-rollover flag: redwood-config set prefix_cache_fallback=true.\  4. If rollout-related (new model variant), rollback to previous variant via canary rollback: redwood-deploy rollback --model <model-id> --version previous.\  5. Validate with synthetic load (curl -sS https://internal-health/model_probe | jq .latency)

- Symptom: Progressive P95 latency increase (SLO class: High)\  
  1. Check batching histogram and queue lengths on serving nodes. Look for sustained queueing (Q > 8ms per request).\  2. Temporarily reduce max_batch_size for impacted model: redwood-ctl model-config set --model <id> max_batch_size=8.\  3. If latency persists, enable local-prefetch cache and measure effect.\  4. If under capacity stress, trigger autoscale burst: redwood-scale trigger --pool <dedicated-pool> --burst 20%.

Severity decision ladder (quick checklist)
- Sev0: Trigger Exec review, page CTO, activate customer war room. Update status page within first 10 minutes.
- Sev1: Page SRE lead and Product on-call. Bridge Operator posts status every 30 minutes.
- Sev2: Triage on-call only; cadence 60–120 minutes for customer comms.

On-call rotation and expectations
- Rotation model: Primary (7-day shift) + Secondary (7-day shadow) per platform region.
- Handover: Daily standup in #oncall-handoff at 09:00 local; handover note must contain outstanding incidents, maintenance windows, and noisy alerts.\- Escalation contacts:
  - Primary on-call: pager (primary), slack DM, phone.
  - Secondary on-call: notified after 15 minutes if acknowledgement not seen.\  - Engineering lead: notified if issue unresolved for 60 minutes or severity upgraded.
- Time commitment: expected to be available within 15 minutes of pager during shift; long-running restoration requires rotation swapping with lead agreement.

Game-day simulation guide (quarterly schedule)
- Frequency: Quarterly full-team simulation + monthly micro-sims for critical subsystems.
- Typical 4-hour game-day agenda:
  1. 0:00 — Inject: synthetic degradation (e.g., region blobstore latency and KV cache evictions).
  2. 0:05 — Pager triggers and primary acknowledges.
  3. 0:10 — Bridge stands up and status page skeleton posted.
  4. 0:20 — Engineering executes runbook or improvises mitigation.
  5. 1:30 — Restore and validate; runbook updates captured.
  6. 2:00 — Post-game retro using postmortem rubric; assign follow-ups.
- Scoring: time-to-ack, time-to-first-status-post, time-to-restoration, and quality of postmortem (rubric score).

Status page and customer comms templates
- Status page cadence: initial acknowledgement within 10 minutes for Sev0/Sev1, subsequent updates every 30 minutes for Sev0 and 60 minutes for Sev1.
- Status update template (short):
  - Title: Partial degradation of inference API in us-west-2\  
  - Incident ID: INC-2025-####\  
  - Time: 2025-07-14T15:10Z\  
  - Summary: We’re investigating elevated 5xx errors impacting inference requests in us-west-2. Root cause under investigation.\  
  - Impact: Some customers experience increased errors and higher latency. Persisting requests may be retried automatically by SDKs.\  
  - Next update: 2025-07-14T15:40Z\  
  - Contacts: support@redwood.ai for account-specific concerns.
- Customer severity email (when incident hits paid customers):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Service Impact (INC-2025-####)\  
  Body: Dear <Customer>,\n\  We are investigating an issue affecting inference latency and error rates for requests routed to us-west-2. Our on-call and platform engineers are actively mitigating the issue. We will provide updates at least every 30 minutes until resolved. For urgent account-level concerns, please reply to this message or reach out to support@redwood.ai.\n\  — The Redwood Inference Team

Postmortem Quality Rubric (acceptance criteria)
- Sections required: Summary, Timeline (UTC), Detection, Impact, Root Cause Analysis, Containment & Recovery steps, Remediation plan, Owner(s), Action items with due dates, Follow-up verification plan.\- Rubric scoring (0-4 scale per criterion):
  1. Completeness (required sections present) — 0..4\  2. Timeline fidelity (timestamps and evidence links) — 0..4\  3. RCA quality (one true root cause, not multiple surface causes) — 0..4\  4. Mitigation clarity (playbook or config changes captured) — 0..4\  5. Remediation tracking (owner & due date assigned) — 0..4\  6. Preventative engineering (tests/monitoring added) — 0..4\- Acceptance threshold: total >= 18 out of 24 for publication to the learning archive. If score < 18, PM/owner must iterate within 5 business days.

Evidence collection checklist
- Collect: alert IDs, raw request IDs, host logs (rotate to secure bucket), metrics query ranges, API traces, and the first-detection signal.\- Standard CLI commands to capture evidence:
  - redwood-logs fetch --service inference --since 2025-07-14T15:00Z --filter "error" > /tmp/inference-errors.log\  - redwood-metrics query --metric request_latency --agg p95 --from 2025-07-14T14:30Z --to 2025-07-14T16:00Z > /tmp/latency-p95.csv\  - redwood-traces export --span inference --txn <trace-id> --out /tmp/trace.json

Governance and SLAs for follow-ups
- High-severity remediation plan posted: within 7 calendar days.\- Code/infra fixes targeted for merge within 30 days and rollout within 60 days unless exception granted by SRE Manager.
- Quarterly summary of published postmortems and outstanding remediations shared with leadership.

Runbook hygiene and ownership
- Each team owning a service must maintain runbooks in this directory with explicit owner and last-verified date.
- Runbooks are validated in every quarterly game-day; failures in runbook efficacy require an immediate runbook update and a follow-up ticket.

Appendix: quick checklists and contact matrix
- Quick triage checklist (for first responder):
  1. Acknowledge and declare bridge.
  2. Identify affected region(s)/model(s).
  3. Confirm severity and page escalation if needed.\ 4. Post initial status.
- Contact matrix (order):
  1. Primary on-call (pager).
  2. Secondary on-call (after 15 min).\ 3. SRE Lead (after 60 min or immediate for Sev0).

Notes and change log
- 2025-02-10: Playbook created by Priya Nair.
- 2025-07-14: Added postmortem rubric and remediation SLAs; updated status templates to require 30-minute cadence for Sev0.
